chapters.title: What it is
lines: Your laptop's on the TV. Or the projector. Or across the room, running the show.
You're not next to it. You don't need to be.
Meet Edgepad version four. An open-source Android app that turns your phone into a trackpad, a remote and a control deck for your laptop. Windows, Mac or Linux.

chapters.title: Setup
lines: A companion app runs on the laptop. Pair once over Bluetooth, like a headset.
No account. No server. No cloud. Your phone talks straight to your laptop.

chapters.title: The trackpad
lines: The middle is a multi-touch trackpad. One finger moves, two scroll and pinch, three switch desktops, four switch apps. Every gesture is remappable.

chapters.title: Corner dials
lines: The corners are dials. Volume, brightness, zoom, video scrubbing. Flip one switch, and four become eight.
The volume syncs both ways. Change it on the laptop, and the dial moves with it.
Whatever's playing shows up on the pad. Pocketing your phone? Lock the trackpad, and the dials and media stay live.

chapters.title: Controls
lines: Tap Controls for the rest.
A full keyboard, with Control, Alt and Shift you can hold or tap.
A gamepad your laptop sees as a real Xbox controller, on Windows and Linux. Your games just see a controller.
A pen that draws live on the laptop's screen. And a signature pad that saves a clean image for any document.
Capture grabs a region, the full screen or a recording, and can save it to your phone.

chapters.title: Macros and clipboard
lines: Macros launch apps, URLs and scripts. Up to fifteen, across as many pages as you need. Bind one to a shape, draw it on the trackpad, and it fires.
Clipboard sync works both ways. Text and images. From the phone, come back to Edgepad and it goes.

chapters.title: Connections and trust
lines: Bluetooth by default. Wi-Fi and USB if you want them.
Connect two laptops at once, and switch between them with a dial. It keeps running in the background.
The laptop holds the trust list. Approve one phone, a few, or revoke them all. Add a six-digit PIN for the first pairing, or for every connection.

chapters.title: Make it yours
lines: Then make it yours. Remap the corners, tune the dials, dark or light, your own background, upright or sideways.

chapters.title: Straight talk
lines: Straight talk: Windows is tested on real hardware. Mac, Linux, Wi-Fi and USB are new and in beta. Expect bugs, and open issues when you find them.

chapters.title: Get it
lines: Edgepad. Free and open source. Use it, fork it, star it. It's on GitHub.
Your laptop, from anywhere in the room.
